audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 is marked Darius in both layers while whys[0] and content.early both say Gnar out-pokes you before Apprehend exists; Levels 3 and 6 are 'Skill' although the same entry says you control them; two-plus items is marked Darius while content.late calls it a skill matchup.
audit.why: Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 units on a 16s cooldown at rank 1 and Hyper gives him move speed — Darius has no answer at level 1. From 3 to first item Apprehend pins a squishy Mini form. Late, Mega windows genuinely even it out.
audit.corrected: Gnar / Darius / Darius / Darius / Darius / Darius / Skill in both layers.
sources: internal contradiction with whys[0] and content.late

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 stage text is the LaTeX fragment 'R = d + a \times Stacks'; the First item stage says 'Force fights on GNAR! (Mega Stun)'s cooldown' without the number.
audit.why: Player-facing copy should not contain a formula fragment, and GNAR! is 90/60/30 seconds — a number that actually changes when you commit.
audit.corrected: Plain-language Level 6 text plus the real GNAR! cooldown at first item.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry calls GNAR! a stun throughout ('GNAR! (Mega Stun)', 'GNAR! stun and knock-up', 'GNAR! double-CC') and labels the wall interaction 'Mega-E'. It also says Mini Gnar 'kites your Decimate slow'.
audit.why: Riot's text: GNAR! throws enemies in a chosen direction and slows them — only an enemy that hits a wall is stunned. The dependable Mega stun is Wallop (W), 7s. The wall interaction belongs to R, not E. And Decimate has no slow at all; Darius's slows are Crippling Strike (W) and Apprehend (E), so the stated reason you fail to stick is the wrong ability.
audit.corrected: GNAR! described as a throw plus slow that only stuns into a wall; Wallop named as the real stun; slow attributed to Crippling Strike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says that fighting in open lane defuses GNAR!.
audit.why: The wall is the condition on the stun, so lane position — not the Rage bar alone — decides whether his ult locks you down.

edits.before: Hemorrhage passive bleed completely overwhelms raw early base stats in any standing fight. Trade on his last-hits but don't chase past the wave.
edits.after: Boomerang Throw pokes from 1100 units on a 16-second cooldown and Hyper walks him out of range. Farm level 1 and start trading once Apprehend is up.

edits.before: Full basic kits unlocked on both sides; spacing out displacements determines the winner. Keep the wave near your tower so Gnar has to walk into pull range.
edits.after: Apprehend answers Hop and Mini Gnar cannot out-bleed you once pinned. Keep the wave near your tower so Gnar walks into pull range on a low Rage bar.

edits.before: Noxian Guillotine deals true damage R = d + a \times Stacks, bypassing defensive items completely. The execute resets on takedowns — all-in windows are now real kill windows.
edits.after: Noxian Guillotine is true damage scaled by Hemorrhage stacks, so Mega Gnar's bulk does not save him. The execute resets on takedowns — all-in windows are now real kill windows.

edits.before: Stridebreaker fixes your stickiness — the run-down you couldn't finish before is now lethal. Force fights on GNAR! (Mega Stun)'s cooldown.
edits.after: Stridebreaker fixes your stickiness — the run-down you couldn't finish before is now lethal. Force fights while GNAR! is down, 60s at rank 2.

edits.before: You stay a side-lane terror but fall off vs grouped teams. Look for flank pulls in fights; one reset chain can win the game.
edits.after: Rage reads decide it: Wallop stuns, GNAR! shoves you into walls. Flank on a low bar and one pull-into-reset chain wins fights.

edits.before: Whiffing Apprehend and then fighting anyway — without the pull you have no engage, and chasing through a wave bleeds you dry.
edits.after: Only an enemy GNAR! throws into a wall is stunned — fight in open lane and his ultimate is a shove and a slow, not a lockdown.

edits.before: You still control the duel — but watch his Rage bar, not his level. If he transforms into Mega Gnar mid-fight his GNAR! stun and knock-up can flip your all-in, so bait or fight when the bar is low, then pull, ramp and Guillotine.
edits.after: You still control the duel — but watch his Rage bar, not his level. In Mega form Wallop stuns on a 7s cooldown and GNAR! shoves you into walls, so bait or fight when the bar is low, then pull, ramp and Guillotine.

edits.before: Transform to Mega and flip fights with GNAR! double-CC
edits.after: Transform to Mega and Wallop-stun you off the pull

edits.before: Two-plus items settles into a skill matchup. Mega Gnar's GNAR! knock-up-plus-stun and AoE burst can win a teamfight outright, and Mini Gnar kites your Decimate slow from range, but a well-timed engage on a low Rage bar still lets you pull and delete him. It comes down to who reads the transform timer better.
edits.after: Two-plus items settles into a skill matchup. Wallop stuns every 7 seconds and GNAR! only locks you down if it slams you into a wall, so fight in open lane; Mini Gnar kites the Crippling Strike slow you stick with. A low-Rage-bar engage still lets you pull and delete him. It comes down to who reads the transform timer better.

edits.before: Level 1-2 is Gnar's: his Q boomerang and hop mobility let him poke you for free before you have E to answer, so respect the early range and don't walk into double-boomerang. From level 3 the lane turns — once E is online you pull Mini Gnar in and your bleed shreds his squishy early form.
edits.after: Level 1 is Gnar's: Boomerang Throw pokes from 1100 units before you have Apprehend to answer, so respect the range and don't walk into a double-boomerang. From level 2-3 the lane turns — once E is online you pull Mini Gnar in and your bleed shreds his squishy early form.

notes: breakdown.wave and breakdown.trading on this entry carry the same PDF-extraction run-on ('Key Mechanical Cooldowns ... How Darius Wins Trades') seen on garen; not touched here. Riot's derived flags tag GNAR! with 'terrain'; the description does not create terrain, so I did not assert it.
